summary: CTRL+SPACE is a mobile-first research platform that makes NASA research on fire and combustion in microgravity easier to explore and understand. It addresses the challenge of improving fire safety in spacecraft by organizing scientific reports, experiment data, and verified research findings in one accessible place. Users can search NASA reports, explore experiments, compare documented results, and use an AI-assisted research feature that provides answers grounded in scientific sources with citations when an AI provider is available. The platform currently organizes 10 research reports, 87 verified passages, and 10 experiments. By making complex research easier to access and trace back to its original sources, CTRL+SPACE helps students and researchers better understand the science needed for safer future space missions.
details:
CTRL+SPACE is a mobile-first research platform designed to help students and researchers explore NASA studies about fire and combustion in microgravity. It addresses the challenge of understanding how fire behaves in spacecraft and how scientific research can contribute to safer space missions.

The platform brings together NASA research reports, verified scientific passages, and structured experiment information in one place. Users can search for research, explore report details, read evidence linked to its original source, and compare documented experiments. The project covers three important areas of spacecraft fire safety: fire prevention, smoke detection, and flame suppression.

One of its main features is an evidence-grounded AI research assistant. It uses BM25 search to retrieve relevant passages from verified NASA reports. When an AI provider is configured, it can generate answers based on the retrieved evidence and provide citations. The system is designed to avoid unsupported answers and identify information that is missing or not reported. Without an AI provider, users can still search and explore the scientific evidence in retrieval-only mode.

Other features include an experiment explorer, side-by-side experiment comparison, a research library, saved collections, personal notes, learning lessons, quizzes, and community discussions. The interface supports English and Arabic, including right-to-left layout, and provides offline access to previously downloaded research.

The platform was developed using Python 3 and Flask for the backend, SQLite for database management, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript ES Modules for the frontend. It uses BM25 for research retrieval, a configurable integration with AI providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama, and Playwright for browser testing. The mobile experience is implemented as a dedicated Progressive Web App (PWA), with Capacitor packaging prepared for Android and iOS. No specialized physical hardware is required.

Our creative approach is combining scientific research discovery, evidence verification, experiment comparison, and AI-assisted explanations in one accessible mobile experience. We considered scientific accuracy, source traceability, missing data, usability on different screen sizes, bilingual accessibility, and offline availability throughout development.

The intended impact is to make complex microgravity combustion research easier to access and understand, helping students and researchers explore the science behind spacecraft fire safety. Future development will focus on expanding the verified research collection, extracting more information from scientific figures and tables, improving AI-assisted search, and completing further native mobile deployment and testing.

CTRL+SPACE is an independent student-developed project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
